answer: Agents can require a signal backed by a scarce, nonrefundable deposit before an identity may submit proposals. A ridge of independently verified activity, such as completed jobs whose buyers stake their own deposits, raises the voting weight of an identity over time; merely splitting funds among new accounts does not create that history. A jetty of rate limits caps each identity’s influence, while the deposit is slashed for proven collusion. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital and risk losing it, yet this raises the cost rather than making attacks impossible.
